risks: The main risk is to the public: a true event dismissed on a checklist or usual day. The safety panel reviews each dismissed true event within a week and can stop the evaluation.
consent: No personal information is used beyond line lists already handled in routine surveillance; the six epidemiologists are informed and agree to the allocation of their duty days; individual consent is not required for program evaluation under the chair's classification.
data: Only alert identifiers, time stamps, syndrome, decision and outbreak linkage are extracted; data stay in the agency's surveillance environment.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: people in care homes and in small rural communities generate small-count signals that are easiest to dismiss. The checklist includes an explicit care home and small-area check, and dismissals are reported by setting and by rural or urban area.
effectiveness: The evaluation shows whether the checklist saves epidemiologist time without harming detection, which decides whether it becomes standard.
efficiency: Uses existing staff and logs; configuration change only.
costs: Analyst time for allocation and analysis within existing roles.
partnerships: Local health units (outbreak confirmation), the laboratory network (reports), and a care home sector representative on the safety panel.
rebPath: Classified by the research ethics committee chair as program evaluation not requiring review (letter REC-2026-PE-07, 2026-09-10); the director approved the evaluation (memo PHA-DIR-2026-31).
limitations: Six epidemiologists in one agency; contamination may persist; missed events too few to compare.
summary: Program evaluation with a safety panel, staff agreement, and equity reporting for care homes and rural areas.
